classification.difficultyReason: Infer the value of one ratio part from the longest piece, then find the total and shortest lengths.

content.prompt: A rope is cut into three pieces whose lengths are in the ratio $1:3:6$. Given that the length of the longest piece is $36\text{ m}$, find:

children.label: a
children.prompt: the length of the original rope

answer.worked:
The longest piece represents $6$ parts.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Length of one part}&=36\div6\\\text{Length of one part}&=6\text{ m}\\\text{Total number of parts}&=1+3+6=10\\\text{Length of original rope}&=10\times6\\\text{Length of original rope}&=60\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the length of the shortest piece of rope

answer.worked:
The shortest piece represents $1$ part.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Length of shortest piece}&=36\div6\\\text{Length of shortest piece}&=6\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
